subtitle: Dhanga-deva and the Waters of Sovereignty

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Dhanga standing between a temple spire and the distant confluence of two great rivers
panels.action: Dhanga-deva Chandela stands in royal armour, one hand resting on the carved plinth of a soaring stone temple and the other extended toward a hazy vision of the Ganga-Yamuna confluence, under a vast, cloud-drifted sky.

dialogue.text: In an age when kings boasted of masters above them, Dhanga-deva erased the overlord’s name, raised Vishvanatha in stone, and walked into the meeting of two rivers to choose his own end.

i18n.hi: जब राजा ऊपर के स्वामियों का गर्व करते थे, धंगदेव ने अधिपति का नाम मिटाया, पत्थर में विश्वनाथ उठाया, और दो नदियों के संगम में जा कर अपना अंत खुद चुना।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscription carved in stone, with Dhanga faintly reflected in polished surface
panels.action: A close view of a Chandela inscription carved in neat Nagari lines on a stone slab, its letters catching the light; in the gleam we faintly see Dhanga’s calm, bearded face as if he studies his own record.

dialogue.text: For generations, Chandela grants had bowed to distant Pratihara emperors; their names flowed through every line of praise. Then, in Dhanga’s records, the imperial names fall suddenly silent.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से चंदेलों की दान-पत्रों में दूर बैठे प्रतिहार सम्राटों के नाम झुकते रहे; हर प्रशंसा-पंक्ति में वे बहते थे। फिर धंग के अभिलेखों में, साम्राज्य के नाम अचानक मौन हो गए।

panels.shot: wide aerial of central India showing Kanauj fading, Kalinjar and Khajuraho rising
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of the plains: Kanauj’s palace complex is shown in softened, crumbling outline, while the rocky fort of Kalinjar and the clustered shrines of Khajuraho glow with new construction and busy movement.

dialogue.text: By the mid-tenth century, Pratihara power frayed; Kanauj’s hold slackened over the Ganga plain. Regional chiefs watched, waited, and weighed how long the old chain would hold.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के मध्य तक प्रतिहार शक्ति घिस गई; कन्नौज की पकड़ गंगा मैदानी इलाकों पर ढीली पड़ गई। प्रांतीय नायक देखते, इंतज़ार करते, और तौलते रहे कि पुरानी ज़ंजीर कब तक टिकेगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dhanga at court, scrolls and priests around him
panels.action: Dhanga sits on a low, carved throne in a Khajuraho hall, counsellors and Brahmana scribes beside him with palm-leaf charters; his hand hovers over a scroll, his brow intent as he listens.

dialogue.speaker: dhanga
dialogue.text: If their arm cannot reach Kalinjar, must my record still reach their name?

i18n.hi: अगर उनकी भुजा कालिंजर तक नहीं पहुँचती, तो क्या मेरे अभिलेख में उनका नाम अब भी पहुँचे?

panels.shot: close-up on scribe’s hand stopping mid-word, Dhanga’s ringed hand blocking
panels.action: A scribe’s stylus pauses just as he begins to incise an overlord’s title on a copper plate; Dhanga’s ringed fingers press lightly yet firmly on the leaf, halting the line.

dialogue.text: Dhanga’s charters no longer called him a feudatory. The overlord’s epithet, once automatic, vanished. In the quiet of the record, Chandela sovereignty spoke louder than any boast.

i18n.hi: धंग के फरमान अब उसे सामंत नहीं कहते। अधिपति का उपनाम, जो कभी अपने आप जुड़ जाता था, गायब हो गया। अभिलेख के सन्नाटे में चंदेल स्वराज्य किसी भी शेख़ी से ज़्यादा गूंज उठा।

panels.shot: wide of Khajuraho building site with temple skeleton rising, Dhanga inspecting
panels.action: On the red earth of Khajuraho, masons and sculptors swarm around the stone skeleton of a great temple; Dhanga, in a simple mantle, walks the site, palm raised toward the upcoming shikhara.

dialogue.text: Freed from formal subordination, Dhanga turned Khajuraho into a royal sacred centre. Inscriptions remember him not only as king, but as the patron whose gifts made shrines and rituals flourish.

i18n.hi: औपचारिक अधीनता से मुक्त होकर, धंग ने खजुराहो को राज-धार्मिक केंद्र बना दिया। अभिलेख उसे सिर्फ राजा नहीं, बल्कि उस दानी संरक्षक के रूप में याद रखते हैं जिसकी भेंटों से मंदिरे और पूजा-पाठ फले।

panels.shot: low-angle on Vishvanatha temple’s half-finished shikhara, architect in foreground
panels.action: From below, the rising tiers of the Vishvanatha temple shikhara frame a master architect, Chhichha, gesturing with a measuring cord, while Dhanga stands at the base, head tilted back to take in the height.

dialogue.text: One inscription sings of Dhanga’s Vishvanatha at Khajuraho, and of Chhichha, the architect whose hands shaped its tower. It is a rare moment when a royal record names the craftsman beside the king.

i18n.hi: एक शिलालेख खजुराहो के धंग-प्रेरित विश्वनाथ की गाथा गाता है, और छिछ्छा उस शिल्पी की, जिसकी हथेलियों ने उसका शिखर गढ़ा। दुर्लभ है कि राज-अभिलेख में राजा के साथ कारीगर का भी नाम दर्ज हो।

panels.shot: reverent close-up of the Marakateshvara linga being installed
panels.action: Priests and artisans carefully lower a dark, polished linga, studded with tiny gleams like embedded gems, into the sanctum pedestal, while Dhanga watches from the doorway, palms joined.

dialogue.text: Within that sanctum, the Vishvanatha inscription recalls a Marakateshvara linga, adorned with emeralds. The text delights in detail: jewels, endowments, the ritual care binding king, deity, and land.

i18n.hi: उसी गर्भगृह के भीतर, विश्वनाथ-शिलालेख मणिमय मरकटेश्वर लिंग का स्मरण करता है। पाठ रत्नों, दान, और उन पूजा-विधियों में रस लेता है जो राजा, देव और धरती को जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: soft-lit interior of sanctum, Dhanga offering gifts
panels.action: In the dim, lamplit core of the temple, Dhanga kneels before the linga, offering a tray of gold and cloth; his face is lined, his hair streaked with grey, his gaze steady and reflective.

dialogue.speaker: dhanga
dialogue.text: Stone will remember what tongues forget.

i18n.hi: ज़ुबानें भूल जाएँगी, पत्थर याद रखेंगे।

panels.shot: map-like high view with a path traced from Kalinjar to Varanasi region
panels.action: A stylised map spreads beneath Dhanga’s sandaled feet, showing Kalinjar and Khajuraho; a faint, glowing trail leads toward the Varanasi region, where a village cluster is marked discreetly.

dialogue.text: Late in his long reign, a copper-plate from Nanyaura appears. Issued in Dhanga’s name, it hints at his reach toward the Varanasi countryside—perhaps control, perhaps a grant made on pilgrimage.

i18n.hi: अपनी लंबी उम्र के उत्तरार्ध में, नन्यौरा की ताम्रपत्र निकलती है। धंग के नाम से निकला यह फ़रमान वाराणसी देहात की ओर उसकी पहुँच का संकेत देता है—शायद नियंत्रण, शायद तीर्थ-यात्रा पर दिया कोई दान।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dhanga granting land to supplicants in a rural setting
panels.action: Under a peepal tree near modest shrines and huts, Dhanga hands a copper plate to a group of Brahmanas and villagers; behind them, the faint silhouette of the Ganga plain suggests distance from his home forts.

dialogue.text: The plate records land gifted with formal care, but does not shout conquest. Later scholars read its place-names cautiously, weighing whether Dhanga ruled here, or only passed as a devout giver.

i18n.hi: पट्ट पर भूमि-दान का ब्योरा सधे हुए ढंग से दर्ज है, पर विजय का शोर नहीं मचता। बाद के विद्वान इन स्थान-नामों को सावधानी से पढ़ते हैं, तौलते हैं कि धंग ने यहाँ राज किया, या बस दानी यात्री बन कर गुज़रा।

panels.shot: wide of Dhanga at Kalinjar fort walls, gazing toward east
panels.action: On the ramparts of Kalinjar, Dhanga stands wrapped in a shawl, looking eastward over hazy plains; behind him, younger warriors train, while priests chant softly beside a small shrine.

dialogue.text: By the time his inscriptions date to the closing years of the tenth century, Dhanga was an elder statesman. His rule had seen shifting alliances, raids, and temple patronage—yet his records stay measured, precise.

i18n.hi: जब उसके अभिलेख दसवीं सदी के अंतिम वर्षों की तिथि लेते हैं, धंग एक बुज़ुर्ग राजनेता है। उसके राज में संधियाँ बदलीं, धावे हुए, मंदिरों को दान बहा—फिर भी उसके अभिलेख संयत और सटीक रहे।

panels.shot: intimate interior of court, Dhanga consulting with advisors about his final journey
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Dhanga sits cross-legged with a small circle of advisors; a travel staff and simple garments lie folded nearby, his crown set aside on a low table.

dialogue.speaker: dhanga
dialogue.text: A king who broke the chain must also choose when to loosen his own grip.

i18n.hi: जो राजा ज़ंजीर तोड़ता है, उसे अपनी पकड़ ढीली करने का समय भी खुद चुनना होता है।

panels.shot: journey montage wide, Dhanga’s small retinue moving along riverbank roads
panels.action: A long line of riverbank paths stretches into the distance as Dhanga, dressed like a pilgrim with a staff and water-pot, walks with a small retinue beside the gleaming ribbon of a great river.

dialogue.text: The Vishvanatha inscription remembers his last journey to Prayaga, where Ganga and Yamuna meet. It says the king abandoned his body in those waters, leaving palace and fort behind.

i18n.hi: विश्वनाथ-शिलालेख उसकी अंतिम प्रयाग-यात्रा को याद करता है, जहाँ गंगा और यमुना मिलते हैं। वह कहता है, राजा ने वहीं जल में शरीर त्याग दिया, महल और दुर्ग पीछे छोड़कर।

panels.shot: epic wide of the Prayaga confluence at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, mist hangs over the vast confluence where two broad rivers merge; Dhanga stands at the sandy bank, the crowd of other pilgrims fading into a blur as he faces the quiet, meeting waters.

dialogue.text: For the inscription’s author, this was no simple bath. In careful verses, he describes Dhanga discarding the body in the holy join of streams, a jala-samadhi placed in ritual memory, not legend.

i18n.hi: लेखक की नज़र में यह साधारण स्नान नहीं था। कसी हुई पंक्तियों में वह धंग को पवित्र संगम में देह छोड़ते दिखाता है—एक जल-समाधि, जो विधि में दर्ज हुई, कथा में नहीं।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Dhanga stepping into the water, serene
panels.action: Water laps at Dhanga’s knees as he steps deeper into the river, face turned slightly upward, eyes closed, his shoulders relaxed in a calm acceptance; the skyline of distant tents and flags blurs behind him.

dialogue.speaker: dhanga
dialogue.text: From overlord’s shadow to the river’s embrace—this, too, is a choice.

i18n.hi: अधिपति की परछाई से नदी की बाँहों तक—यह भी तो एक चुनाव है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from rippling confluence to the silhouette of Khajuraho’s shikhara
panels.action: The image of the rippling confluence slowly blends into the silhouette of the Vishvanatha shikhara against the sky, as if the waters and the temple are joined across distance and time.

dialogue.text: Dhanga’s body vanished into the rivers, but his absence speaks in what his records do not say, in temples that still stand, and in a sovereign’s choice to end, as he ruled, on his own terms.

i18n.hi: धंग का शरीर नदियों में समा गया, पर उसकी ग़ैरहाज़िरी बोलती है—उसमें जो अभिलेख नहीं कहते, उन मंदिरों में जो आज भी खड़े हैं, और उस संप्रभु के चुनाव में जिसने अंत भी उसी तरह किया, जैसे राज किया—अपनी शर्तों पर।

subtitle_i18n.en: Dhanga-deva and the Waters of Sovereignty
